reasons: The redline delivers the preferred position: an express Client right to terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' written notice, refund of prepaid fees for the post-termination period, no early-termination fee or minimum-fee charge, and an explicit bar on TrueLink terminating for convenience mid-term, while leaving the mutual end-of-term non-renewal right in Section 13 intact.

The failed 'Customer convenience termination present' check is a false negative from alias matching: the contract uses 'Client' (the resolved Customer alias) and the redline plainly states 'Client may terminate this Agreement for convenience ... upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice'.

The 0.729 change ratio on p0079 is justified: the original clause was a service-continuation mechanic with an indeterminate 30-60 day notice window tied to a non-existent 'Section 4', so a rewrite is the only way to create a definite convenience right; the redline still preserves the substance that TrueLink continues services through the effective date and is paid for them.
Deviation classification is fair - the existing text implies a Client election but lacks an express without-cause right, a fixed notice period, and any refund/no-penalty protection.

The Section 13 cross-reference fix (Section 12 -> Section 14) is a 0.043-ratio, in-scope correction needed for the termination right to operate, and the comment accurately explains the change and offers the 60-day fallback in the required tone.

Minor, non-disqualifying: the comment's assertion that Section 12 is the indemnity section cannot be confirmed from the supplied text - worth a quick check before sending, but the correction to the termination section is clearly right.
